[2018-11-26 14:27] thinscallops : Question; If a team runs a high octane OFFENSE which is better? Pressure, zone, or man 2 man?
[2018-11-26 17:55] thinscallops : Goshdarnit*#% I had my extend defense set to +5 and South Carolina still went 11-24 on shooting threes, and of course they won by three points by shooting a three on their last possesion.

[2018-11-26 23:05] crazyli825 : I can't speak on this game's philosophy, but I would assume you need to pressure a high octane offense. Force them to make turnovers. Man vs. Zone doesn't really address this. You play Man if you're confident that your players at each position have better defense than the offensive capabilities of who they'll be matched up against. If you don't think you can beat all (or most) of them straight-up, you'll want to use zone so your guys can work together to cover potential weaknesses.
[2018-11-26 23:06] crazyli825 : Rather than stick like glue to a guy of the same position, zone goes with the approach of: if the guy with the ball comes near me, I'm going to guard him" It's best executed with a solid defense in which everyone has sufficient defensive ability for their zone (i.e.: Bigs with good ID and guards with good PD)
[2018-11-26 23:08] crazyli825 : A better example of when zone might work better I guess is say the other team's point guard is really good at driving to the hoop and scoring inside, despite being a guard. Your PG has great PD because that's what you look for in a guard, but crappy ID. This might mean that ones the opposing guard gets inside, your man fails to stop him and he gets easy inside baskets. If you played zone, your C and PF (who hopefully have really strong ID) will step up and make it much more difficult for that guard to successfully score.
[2018-11-26 23:09] crazyli825 : But zone defense is less tight than sticking to a single guy.
[2018-11-26 23:09] crazyli825 : So it's really all on how well your matching up.
[2018-11-26 23:11] thinscallops : Kinda along the ones of what I was thinking.

[2019-04-17 03:19] infinite_tea : Yeah, it's definitely a cap.
[2019-04-17 03:19] infinite_tea : He probably called it a target because that's how many minutes they aim to get -- pending foul trouble.
[2019-04-17 03:21] infinite_tea : 5* and 10* is mainly not recommended for two reasons: 1. A player may play so infrequently that you could have instead used a redshirt. 2. If it comes down to a backup being set at 5*, and the starter gets in trouble and there ends up being 10 minutes that need to be played... well, the backup is capped at 5*, so the CPU will only play them for 5 and then select the next player randomly to fill in (well, according to CPU best fit criteria). So essentially, you're capping a player that wouldn't need capped.
[2019-04-17 03:23] infinite_tea : If you have a depth chart with 3 deep at a position, minutes set as: PG1 = 24 minutes PG2 = 5 minutes PG3 = 15 minutes  Then I think it'll work fine. But if you're using it for the last player on your rotation, such as... PG1 = 24 minutes PG2 = 15 minutes PG3 = 5 minutes  Then you might as well set PG3 higher, because he will only get the minutes that are left over by PG1 and PG2 (in this case, it would be 1).

[2020-01-07 01:43] furysk : 540/13 = 41.5 contacts per player
[2020-01-07 01:44] furysk : is redshirting everyone likely to punish you more than 10 contacts per player?  probably not.
[2020-01-07 01:44] furysk : although if you bounce between 1 contact 1 scholarship guys in there, and get ti down to like 660/10 and 535/10, the margin is even greater for you to redshirt everyone.

[2020-07-03 07:23] .divac : Guys, how you insert into a forum post link with a name? For example, link to my profile but named it Divac.
[2020-07-03 10:04] gards710 : <@!718372571250163763> step 1) write the text. In this case, it will be "Divac". 2) Highlight/select that section of text. 3) when writing a post, there will be a button in the bar where you write the main body of your post (the B, I, U and other buttons). This button is the fourth button, to the right of the U, and looks like a chain link. 4) Click that and copy-paste the link of the URL of the page of your profile (http://www.brokenbat.org/profile/12586). 5) Click OK.
